Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then apply the fish-control bookshelf protocol and inspect both required wake views before touching the policy. I’ll keep the implementation to one candidate and update both the candidate notes and reusable guidance as part of the same evidence trail.

The inherited bank says the current carrier already captures, while several “relief” and route-residual ideas preserved attractive wakes but broke the target approach. I’m now separating genuine route differences from executable duplicates, then I’ll choose one bounded mechanism whose effect can be falsified by the next rollout.

The assigned parent supplied the decisive negative control: posterior-wave attenuation stayed self-propelled and coherent, yet turned upward, bottomed out at 3.9248 L, and exited at 26.21 T. That rejects posterior-specific wave reallocation around this carrier. I’m consulting the bookshelf now because the inherited run is exactly the kind of mechanism failure the transfer protocol is meant to redirect.

The shelf transfer points to a clean next test: keep the traveling wave entirely unchanged and strengthen only target-signed mean curvature when the target becomes broadside. A completed inherited rollout already exercised that gate and still captured; I’m documenting the visual diagnosis and falsification boundary before applying the mechanism to the better mean-distance carrier.

The candidate now preserves every wave term and adds only the evidence-backed broadside curvature layer. I’ve also converted the assigned parent’s failure into a reusable bidirectional “do not reallocate the posterior wave” boundary. Next I’m running the mandated contract checks and a small state-feedback ablation—no CFD.

The provenance check found a rendered-workspace defect: the same assigned parent is marked twice in `README.md`, so parent resolution is ambiguous even though both entries are identical. The mandated checker requires one marker; I’m removing only the redundant second marker, then rerunning all checks.

All mandated checks now pass after exposing the pinned Julia launcher: guidance provenance/materiality, policy contract/schema, and solver edit boundaries. The focused dry ablation also confirms exact parent behavior below the broadside gate, a real action change above it, reflection symmetry, and bounded finite commands.

Produced exactly one Phase 2 candidate: a bounded broadside curvature reserve layered onto the successful envelope-redistribution carrier while preserving the posterior traveling wave.

- [Candidate policy](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- [Evidence, bookshelf transfer, and falsification notes](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [Reusable posterior-wave negative boundary and broadside-reserve lesson](guidance/control_experience.md:106)

All required checks pass: guidance materiality, Julia policy contract/schema, solver boundary, reflection symmetry, inactive-gate parent equivalence, active-gate differentiation, and bounded finite outputs. No CFD was run.
